text: Lewis analyzes 'Humphrey might have won the election' using counterpart theory. On this analysis the claim is true if and only if what holds?
choices: Humphrey himself exists in another possible world and wins the election there.
Some individual who is a counterpart of Humphrey (resembling him closely enough in the relevant respects) wins the election in some world.
The proposition that Humphrey wins is a member of some maximal consistent set of propositions.
In the closest world where Humphrey runs, he wins.
explanation: Because Lewis rejects transworld identity (no concrete individual is part of two spatiotemporally isolated worlds), the modal claim is made true by a counterpart: an individual in another world who is suitably qualitatively similar to Humphrey and who wins there. Option 0 asserts the very transworld identity Lewis denies, so it is the tempting but incorrect reading; the winner is Humphrey's counterpart, not Humphrey.
